title: Keep a reader with no match
summary: OPTIONAL MATCH keeps the earlier row even when the optional connection is missing.
introduction: OPTIONAL MATCH keeps the earlier row even when the optional connection is missing. Your task: Explain why Sam should still appear in a list of all readers.
learningObjectives: Explain why Sam should still appear in a list of all readers.
Explain the example for keep a reader with no match

blocks.text: OPTIONAL MATCH keeps the earlier row even when the optional connection is missing. Missing values appear as null.
Use Neo4j 5+ locally with Neo4j Browser or another Cypher editor. These queries use fictional cma-prefixed ids. Cypher is not SQL and does not run in this site's SQL playground.

blocks.code:
MERGE (r:Reader {id:'cma-r2'}) SET r.name='Sam'
WITH r OPTIONAL MATCH (r)-[:READ]->(b:Book) RETURN r.name,b.title;
blocks.title: Keep a reader with no match

blocks.text: Read the code step by step

items: `MERGE` matches or creates the specified graph pattern. Use a stable identity pattern, then SET changing properties.
`OPTIONAL MATCH` keeps the earlier row when its optional pattern is absent, using null for missing values.
`MATCH` finds the described graph pattern. Labels and arrow direction narrow the connections being followed.

blocks.text: Sam is returned with a null book title if no READ relationship exists.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: A regular MATCH would remove the row when the pattern has no match. Choose based on the question you need to answer.

blocks.title: Your small task
blocks.text: Explain why Sam should still appear in a list of all readers.
